stockholders, as we reflect on 2025 and look ahead to 2026 and beyond, nurix enters its next chapter with a pivotal development program in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (cll) underway. in addition, we are expanding opportunities in inflammation and immunology (i&i) and deepening our partnered pipeline. our focus remains clear: to establish degrader-based medicines at the forefront of patient care in oncology and autoimmune disease. tremendous progress in 2025: from proof of concept to pivotal trials 2025 marked a year of strategic transition for nurix as bexobrutideg, our lead bruton’s tyrosine kinase (btk) degrader, advanced from clinical proof of concept into registrational development in relapsed/refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (cll), the most common leukemia in adults. at the 67th american society of hematology (ash) annual meeting, we presented maturing phase 1a/1b data in heavily pretreated cll patients that underscore bexobrutideg’s potential best-in-class profile. in the phase 1a cohort that consisted of patients who had received many prior lines of treatment, bexobrutideg achieved a remarkable objective response rate (orr) of 83.0%, including two complete responses, with a median progression-free survival (pfs) of 22.1 months and a median duration of response of 20.1 months across all doses tested. data from the randomized phase 1b cohort comparing 200 mg and 600 mg once-daily dosing demonstrated higher response rates and a favorable trend toward longer pfs at the 600 mg dose. these results supported the 600 mg dose as the recommended phase 2 dose in accordance with fda’s project optimus. importantly, bexobrutideg was well tolerated, demonstrating a consistent safety profile across dose levels, with no dose-limiting toxicities, no systemic fungal infections, and no grade 4 infections. we also reported encouraging phase 1 data in waldenström macroglobulinemia (wm), a type of non-hodgkin lymphoma, achieving a 75.0% orr with a median follow-up of 8.1 months. notably, neither median duration of response nor pfs had been reached, indicating that patients continue to benefit from therapy over time. collectively, these results position bexobrutideg as a potentially transformative once-daily, oral therapy for patients with b-cell malignancies. beyond bexobrutideg, we continued to advance our broader oncology pipeline, reflecting nurix’s ability to apply its degrader expertise across multiple programs. zelebrudomide, our dual btk and cereblon neosubstrate degrader, progressed through dose escalation with the new chirally controlled drug form. nx-1607, our oral cbl-b inhibitor, generated additional monotherapy signals of efficacy with a disease control rate of 49.3% across doses and tumor types as well as supportive translational data in solid tumors, demonstrating dose-dependent target engagement and peripheral immune activation. daybreak™ and the path to registration the daybreak-201 phase 2 study in relapsed/refractory cll is designed as a pivotal trial to support accelerated approval in the united states. it is enrolling adult patients who have progressed after all approved agents, including a covalent btk inhibitor, a bcl-2 inhibitor, and a non-covalent btk inhibitor. these patients currently have few meaningful treatment options remaining. we also announced plans for daybreak-306, a phase 3 trial that will test bexobrutideg head-to-head against the latest approved btk non-covalent inhibitor, pirtobrutinib. the trial is designed to not only enable full approval of bexobrutideg in the united states and other major markets, but also to generate practice-changing data that compares the removal of cancer-driving proteins versus merely inhibiting its enzymatic function. stat6 and irak4: building a differentiated i&i portfolio stat6 is a key transcription factor regulating type 2 inflammation. our collaboration with sanofi is focused on targeted degradation of stat6 as an approach to modulating il-4/il-13–driven pathways compared with antibody or inhibitor strategies. in 2025, sanofi exercised its option to extend its license for our stat6 program, including on a development candidate, nx-3911, which currently is in investigational new drug (ind) enabling studies. irak4 is a key kinase that regulates immune cell activity. in 2025, gs-6791 demonstrated potent and sustained irak4 degradation, robust inhibition of il-1 and il-36 signaling, and meaningful efficacy in an animal model of table of contents atopic dermatitis. gilead and nurix presented this preclinical data at the 2025 european academy of dermatology and venereology congress. also in 2025, gs-6791 began a comprehensive, first-in-human phase 1 study in healthy volunteers. financial strength and operational discipline we ended fiscal 2025 with $592.9 million in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. in october 2025, we completed a $250.0 million underwritten registered offering with participation from leading healthcare-focused institutional investors, significantly strengthening our balance sheet and enabling accelerated execution across pivotal clinical programs and pipeline expansion. throughout 2025, our collaborations with gilead, sanofi, and pfizer continued to validate the breadth and scalability of our del-ai™ platform while providing meaningful nondilutive capital. in 2025, we recognized $84.0 million in revenue from these partners and remain eligible for up to $6.1 billion in future fees and milestones, plus royalties on product sales. in oncology, our degrader antibody conjugate (dac) collaboration with pfizer achieved multiple preclinical milestones that demonstrated the feasibility of dacs as a next-generation antibody-drug conjugate modality. in all our collaborations, we maintain highly valuable option rights to join our partners in co-development and co-commercialization in the united states, rights that are triggered after clinical data is obtained from trials funded and managed by our partners. such optionality provides us with the ability to selectively and cost-effectively develop our product pipeline in alignment with established leaders in the fields of oncology and i&i. looking ahead to 2026: advancing to phase 3 in oncology and expanding into i&i the central theme for 2026 is advancing bexobrutideg to phase 3 while also broadening the bexobrutideg clinical program to include selected i&i indications. btk sits at a critical intersection of b-cell receptor, toll-like receptor, and fc-receptor signaling, making it a compelling target in antibody-mediated autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. while existing btk inhibitors validate aspects of this biology, they address only the kinase function of btk and may be limited by off-target effects. bexobrutideg is designed to catalytically degrade btk, eliminating both its kinase and scaffolding functions and enabling deeper and more durable pathway suppression at low, free plasma concentrations. we believe this profile may offer a more effective and safe therapeutic option for chronic autoimmune diseases where sustained control of pathogenic b-cell and myeloid signaling must be balanced with long-term tolerability. 2026 catalysts and strategic priorities as we enter 2026, our focus centers on four major priorities: •
